title: Decouple load-generator from eval-orchestration; introduce deterministic workload plugins
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: The current evaluation pipeline mixes synthetic load generation (locally built scripts in /harness/loadgen) with orchestration logic that schedules, aggregates, and reports perf regressions. This has caused multiple problems: flaky nightly runs, duplicated workload definitions across repos, brittle CI steps that break on minor dependency upgrades, and difficulty running targeted local reproductions for regressions.

Goal: Refactor the perf/eval harness so that the load-generator is a small, well-documented, versioned component with a plugin API for workload definitions (scenario files), and the orchestration layer (eval-runner) consumes standardized artifacts rather than executing ad-hoc scripts. Make runs deterministic (seedable pseudo-randomness), reduce flakiness, and simplify dependency upgrades.

Scope & deliverables:
- Extract loadgen into a standalone package under infra/perf-loadgen with a stable CLI and Python API.
- Define a workload plugin spec (yaml) with fields for model, prompt-set, sequence_length_distribution, qps_profile, and deterministic_seed.
- Implement two reference plugins: k6-compatible HTTP driver and a lightweight in-process harness for fast unit perf checks.
- Update eval-orchestration to accept pre-built workload artifacts (tar.gz with plugin + fixtures) and to validate sha256 of artifacts before running.
- Add a nightly perf-regression CI job that runs the orchestration against the dedicated perf cluster and writes results to Grafana/InfluxDB and to the perf-dashboard S3 bucket.
- Upgrade locust -> 2.9.1 and k6 -> 0.45.1 as part of separate dependency PRs, with compatibility shims for existing scripts.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Plugin spec is intentionally small to avoid chasing feature parity with every internal ad-hoc script. Heavy or custom logic should live in plugins, not the runner.
- Deterministic seeds improve reproducibility but may hide timing-related flakiness; we will run a subset of tests in non-deterministic mode during canary windows.
- Shipping a lightweight in-process harness favors developer iteration speed; full cluster load must still be validated with the k6 driver.

Migration plan:
1) Create perf-loadgen repo skeleton and migrate two canonical scripts (chat_long_seq and batch_embedding) as plugins. (ENG-15733-A)
2) Land API and CLI, publish internal pip package (artifact registry) tagged perf-loadgen@0.1.0. (ENG-15733-B)
3) Update eval-orchestration to accept artifacts, implement validation and shims. (ENG-15733-C)
4) Run end-to-end smoke on staging perf cluster; iterate on flakiness checklist. (ENG-15733-D)
5) Flip nightly perf-regression job and retire legacy CI steps. (ENG-15733-E)

Acceptance criteria:
- perf-loadgen publishes an internal package with README and 2 example plugins.
- Orchestration consumes artifact and returns deterministic run results given the same workload artifact and seed.
- Nightly job completes in <4h for full perf regression matrix with <10% historical variance in median latency for stable workloads.
- CI failure thresholds are documented and enforced via perf-alerts (Grafana alert + Slack).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Upgrading locust/k6 might introduce behavioral differences. Mitigation: compatibility shims and parallel runs for 2 weeks before switching traffic; keep old Docker images for quick rollback.
- Risk: Plugins become another place for unreviewed scripts. Mitigation: add a pre-merge linter and require CHANGES.md and a smoke test artifact.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- Grafana perf/regression dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/perf/benchmark-regressions
- Perf artifacts S3: s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/nightly/2025-*
- CI job: gitlab-ci/perf-regression-nightly (runs in the perf-tenant project)

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Perf+Harness+Plugin+Spec
- Draft perf-loadgen repo (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-loadgen/pull/42
- Eval-orchestration change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-orchestration/pull/2890
- Flakiness runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FlakeRunbook

Rollout timeline:
- Feb 10 - Feb 24: extraction + unit tests (in progress)
- Feb 25 - Mar 7: orchestration adapter + staging runs
- Mar 8 - Mar 14: parallel nightly runs (old + new) and rollback window
- Mar 15: cutover to new nightly job if stable

Estimated effort: 8 points across 2 engineers (Marco Li primary, Sofia Martinez review), 2 weeks calendar working in parallel with dependency upgrade PRs.
